tier_reason: First-party README benchmark stays tier C; its printed output has been unchanged since tag 2.0.0 (May 2016), so the numbers describe args 2.0.0, not the current 6.6.0.

corrections.caveats: README timings (0.895472 / 1.45001 / 1.98972 s) are byte-identical since 2.0.0 (May 2016) and measure the pre-4.0.0 API; never re-run on 6.6.0, which adds per-registration duplicate-flag detection (quadratic construction inside the timed loop). Single machine, no CPU or flags.

tier_reason: Tier C stays (third-party Python-wrapper README, no C/C++ rival); datetime truncation bug and harness notes recorded.

corrections.caveats: python-xlsxio README (about June 2020, 9-star wrapper, no CPU/compiler/versions): about 5.8x vs openpyxl read-only on a 100,000-row file, C vs pure Python only; xlsx2csv row is a second openpyxl run; untyped row compares raw strings with typed values. xlsxioread_sheet_next_cell_datetime truncates instead of rounding (about 36% of %.16g-written datetimes read 1 s early, simulated); next_cell_int uses sscanf %i; case-insensitive sharedstrings matching may load no strings for prefixed <x:sst>. Open crashes #151, #136, #123; styles unparsed (#19); CMake 4 broken (#147). Security fixes 2026-09-24 (#150) and 2026-06-28 (#148).

tier_reason: The only readable harness builds Spicy at -O3 against binpac at -O0 and its single Spicy win compares different grammars, so no valid like-for-like number exists; Spicy is slower than binpac on every comparable unit (3.7x-4.2x, understated). Directional, not faster.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Not faster: evantypanski/spicy-performance (2025) has Spicy WithUnit 14.087 s vs binpac 3.809 s and Regex 10.228 vs 0.378 s even with Spicy at -O3 and binpac at -O0; the BytesUntil 'win' (0.286 vs 1.635 s) compares bytes &until against a per-element uint8[] vector and is not like for like. The 2026 Zeek post's snippet numbers read as seconds (WithUnit 9.357 s, about 1.5x faster than 2025, derived), still about 2x behind binpac.
corrections.caveats: Harness: Spicy built with spicy-config --cxxflags (-O3 -DNDEBUG), binpac with bare clang++ (-O0); committed bench.cc input differs from the README run; binpac regex row from an out-of-repo Zeek plugin. Regex captures by default (&nosub cuts 10 s to about 3 s, issue #1986); fiber-stack exhaustion for large units before 1.17; thread races fixed in 1.17. zeek.org blocked.

tier_reason: The only number is an unmeasured '~200x' release-notes line against vcflib's own crashing zig path, and the measured tool has genotype-renumbering and FORMAT-truncation bugs in its output (bug-in-measured-path precedent). Directional only.

corrections.caveats: '~200x faster on large VCFs' from the unreleased RELEASE_NOTES section (commit 779cf28): no harness, input, timings or hardware; baseline is vcflib's own zig vcfcreatemulti (use-after-free fixed the same week, now off by default, C++ driver deep-copies each Variant). Output bugs: --norm-multiallelic renumbers genotypes wrongly (offset always equals the window index; repo's own regression file shows 0|1 written as 0|2), and FORMAT is truncated to GT (DS/GP dropped). Plain-text input only; strict validator aborts on the first bad line; ALTPROBLEM records violate the spec. Loose fit for csv-tabular.
